pages.text: Both blocks burn flammable fluids: LPG, butane, propane, hydrogen, furnace gas, crude oil, heavy oil, gasoline, diesel, naphtha, kerosene, creosote and lubrication oil. Neither one needs an exhaust.

$(l)Flarestack$()$(br)The flarestack destroys what you pump into it, with a tall flame. Use it on the products your refinery makes but you do not need yet.$(li)Holds $(item)2500 mB$().$(li)Burns $(item)30 mB per tick$(), or $(item)100 mB per tick$() while it holds more than 1000 mB.$(li)Gives off light level 15 while burning.

$(l)Gas lamp$()$(br)A light source that needs no wiring at all.$(li)Holds $(item)4000 mB$() of any of the fluids above.$(li)Burns about $(item)1 mB per second$(), so a full lamp lasts over an hour.$(li)Gives light level 15 while fuelled, and stays lit for 5 seconds after the last drop.
Gas lamps are a good use for small leftovers such as the 10 mB of naphtha per crude oil run, or the creosote from coke ovens.
